claim_summary: DCATS uses metadata-guided dataset proposals and validation-error feedback to refine auxiliary-series selection for forecasting, evaluated through warm-started model fine-tuning.

claim_evidence.quote:
Each proposal is then evaluated by the forecasting module, which
trains models using the sub-dataset and reports performance on
the validation dataset.

Using the validation performance, the LLM-agent
provides a new set of proposals for the next evaluation round,
typically refining the winning strategy from the previous iteration.

modules.name: Warm-started forecasting proposal evaluator
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK matches: this candidate-subset evaluator integrates model pretraining, discord filtering, fine-tuning, and forecasting validation. A different task family requires redesigning its model output and performance criterion. Its numerical-series filtering implements processing, but forecasting-specific evaluation takes precedence over GTS.
rubric_path: R1:contributed - integration of warm-started candidate fitting, filtering, and forecasting evaluation; cited models and discord algorithms are not separate contributions
R2:Harness - trains external forecasting models, not the LLM
R3_1_TSK:yes - evaluates candidate data by forecasting performance

evidence.quote:
The forecasting module trains time series forecasting models using
the sub-dataset and evaluates their performance on the validation
set.

To enhance model convergence speed, we first train a foundation
model [12, 20, 24, 25] using all available time series data before user
queries.

We then use the sub-dataset proposed by the LLM-agent to
fine-tune the foundation model when testing different proposals.

To
further refine the data before fine-tuning, we remove the 10% most
anomalous data from the sub-dataset using discord-based anomaly
detection methods [21, 26].

task_performance.quote:
The DCATS framework consistently improved performance across
all tested methods, with an average improvement of 6% across all
queries, models, and metrics.

notes: Final temporal_validity corrects the blind record's permissive reading: lines 402-404 report a 6:2:2 split and training/validation-only optimization with held-out test reporting, but do not establish chronological splitting, temporal leakage control, or metadata availability cutoffs. Ordinary test separation alone does not establish the R10 temporal contract. Forecasting models and discord detection are existing components; only their evaluator integration is counted. Anomaly removal is internal preprocessing, not an evaluated anomaly-detection task. Metadata neighbor sets are inputs to the forecasting search, not a separately established reusable temporal retrieval contribution. Proposal explanations are qualitative analyses, not checks of tool-call or execution validity. The evaluator is newly recorded because it is a separately described component, rather than splitting or renaming the existing proposal-loop mechanism.

Replace Planning and Workflow and Control, Verification, and Feedback with Planning and Orchestration.

This supports forecasting-specific orchestration and experiment context, not reusable cross-episode evolution. Lines 298-313 separately specify the evaluator's warm-start, filtering, fine-tuning, and validation integration; its existing forecasting models and discord algorithms are not standalone contributions.
